To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hippocampus is necessary for the retrieval of spatial memories, and that retrieval-induced reconsolidation of these memories requires protein synthesis in the hippocampus.

(1) the protein synthesis inhibitor, anisomycine, administered into the CA1 region of the dorsal hippocampus after context memory retrieval, impairs retention of context memory in the fear conditioning paradigm; (2) this postretrieval anisomycin-induced memory impairment is not due to an anisomycin effect on retrieval; and (3) the postretrieval effect is not due to a general impairment of memory consolidation.

Postretrieval administration of anisomycin into the basolateral amygdala impairs retention of fear conditioning, but not extinction of fear conditioning, and that this impairment is blocked by the protein synthesis inhibitor rapamycin.
